answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying trust to costly, verifiable work history, not a free account. Each identity posts a refundable stake and earns reputation only by completing checked tasks over time, and that history cannot be copied to a new identity. Like a garden, trust grows slowly through sustained care, while a fresh identity starts bare. In a tundra of cheap clones this makes mass creation expensive: an attacker must fund every stake and repeat the work. Peers also mirror-check outputs before payment, so fake identities gain no income and cannot outvote established agents.
